_comment: Named I1 tolerances, per class: the maximum absolute difference per channel and the largest per-channel mean over the whole image, between the Windows decode (WIC + policy) and the Mac ImageIO oracle (macOS 27, Version 27.0.1 Build 26A434). Measured on the corpus of this folder (20 runs identical), rounded up ONCE to the digits shown. docs/sr1-decisions.md G34-G37 give the reasons. These classes are measured, not fitted: the calibration and gating sets are the same files (the one-set limit is stated in G37).

jpeg-444.reason: different IDCT and rounding in WIC's JPEG decoder and Apple's: 4:4:4 isolates it (no chroma upsampling)

jpeg-422.reason: IDCT plus horizontal chroma upsampling (the two decoders use different upsampling filters)

jpeg-420.reason: IDCT plus 2x2 chroma upsampling; the maximum sits on hard colour edges where the upsampling filters differ most

jpeg-cmyk.reason: CoreGraphics converts CMYK through its colour-managed Generic CMYK space; WIC's JPEG decoder returns CMYK that the format converter turns into RGB with a plain formula; the red channel carries nearly all of the difference. Not fitted: CMYK JPEG is rare and the Mac conversion is not reproducible from a published profile.

jpeg-p3.reason: JPEG decode difference (4:4:4, q100) plus the matrix/TRC conversion's rounding

p3.reason: matrix/TRC conversion in double precision against CoreGraphics' conversion: 1 level where the two round differently

thumbnail.reason: the host's area-average (box) filter on premultiplied alpha against ImageIO's own thumbnail filter (and, for ICO entries, the scaled entry): different filters; the maxima sit on one-pixel-wide transparent edges of tiny thumbnails (8 px). I2 fits the filters and states the real resampling tolerance.
